newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse pins foreign hopes on computers.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse pins foreign hopes on computers.

text.p: The Nigerian Stock Exchange on Tuesday commissioned a computerised clearing system it hopes will clear the way for a rush of foreign investment.
Stock exchange president Pascal Dozie said the commissioning of the Central Securities Clearing System (CSCS) would lift constraints to the inflow of foreign capital.
"I am bold enough to say the exchange is ready. We will from now on play the enhancing role of a major facilitator in foreign investment inflow into Nigeria," he said.
Interested foreign investors have said the slow pace of Nigeria's clearing system is one reason why they have not put their money into sub-Saharan Africa's largest economy.
Dozie said that when the government introduced laws to appeal to foreign investors in 1995 the antiquated mechanisms of the exchange were unable to meet the challenge.
Among the problems the new system is expected to eliminate are the difficulties associated with transferring shares and producing new certificates.
Services carried out manually over several months should now take only five working days.
"Not only should this increase foreign investment, but it is going to help increase day to day trading as well and make it much more responsive," said one trader.
Daily turnover on the exchange is rarely more than one percent of total market capitalisation which on Monday stood at 379 billion naira ($4.46 billion).
Dozie said the CSCS would provide a central depository for all share certificates of quoted companies as well as settlement and custodian sevices for local and foreign instruments.
He called on the military government to repeal a law requiring physical possession of share certificates to be taken as the only legal proof of ownership.
The much delayed project began in 1989 with the help of the U.N. Development Programme, but suffered from cash shortages and tangled bureaucracy.
The management of the stock exchange said the system would become fully operational from Monday when all stockbroking houses should have submitted their trading documents and bank accounts.
Foreign investment in Nigerian shares grew to $32 million in December 1996 from $1.1 million a year earlier, according to stock exchange figures.
